description:
## Goal

Complete one coherent Kernel foreign-boundary cutover. Public Fz wrappers call ordinary private declarations naming real C exports. Arithmetic foreign functions return failures as data; one Fz helper chooses the existing loud panic. Native arithmetic keeps scalar machine operations and allocation-free result/status transport.

The optimization and ABI changes are part of this ticket, not a future repair. Do not first land boxed arithmetic or a native C-call regression and promise to undo it later. This ticket remains one commit and one close; the internal steps below are a TDD sequence, not separately shippable partial ABI changes.

## Approved source and foreign contract

```fz
extern "C" defp fz_op_add_ii(integer, integer) :: {integer, boolean}

defp arithmetic_error(), do: panic(:badarith)

def (a :: integer) + (b :: integer) do
  case fz_op_add_ii(a, b) do
    {result, false} -> result
    {_, true} -> arithmetic_error()
  end
end
```

- Use existing syntax, lexical FunctionId resolution, source semantic contracts, World facts, tuple transport and return lanes. No intrinsic syntax, synthetic declaration, name-derived semantic contract, new tuple-return subsystem, or display-string authority.
- Only `extern "C" defp` and `extern "fz" defp` are accepted. Public extern declarations remain rejected pending deliberate public-FFI/capture policy. Private declarations do not enter ModuleInterface; ordinary public wrappers and their captures retain ordinary callable identity.
- Both ABI labels call C exports. `C` passes exactly the declared arguments. `fz` prepends current Process* using the existing ABI convention. Context-free helpers use `C`; context-dependent helpers use the truthful existing convention.
- Source export name equals the real physical export name. Keep the completed rename/removal scope: fz_self, fz_make_ref, fz_send, fz_spawn, fz_make_resource; remove obsolete _raw/_ref aliases and spawn_opt. Keep spawn/1; remove spawn/2 and heap-hint plumbing. Do not add other spawn forms.
- pid, ref and cpointer retain typed builtin identities. Derive physical classifications from resolved types, never their rendered spellings.

## Aggregate ABI: exact v1 scope

Fz already has decomposed tuple returns. The missing feature is adapting C aggregate returns into those lanes.

- For an `extern "C"` result, a fixed two-field tuple whose fields are integer, float or boolean denotes a C struct returned by value, fields in tuple order. Support every pairing of those scalar fields, not a name-gated arithmetic-only shape.
- Physical scalar mapping: integer = int64_t; float = double; boolean = uint64_t restricted to 0/1. `boolean` is the sole Fz spelling. This is explicitly NOT C _Bool/Rust bool. Use matching C declarations and Rust repr(C) structs. Convert between this wire boolean and existing Fz boolean/condition lanes without an AnyValueRef box. Fz raw atom IDs are not wire booleans: explicitly map false/true to 0/1 and back at each scalar or aggregate field; never bitcast the atom ID as the flag.
- Audit every affected scalar-boolean declaration and real runtime export before changing the mapping; update both sides atomically. A declaration already spelling boolean is not evidence that its current export returns a raw boolean. Comparisons returning booleans participate in this cutover. Do not globally relabel integer-returning 0/1 helpers (for example fz_bitstring_is_binary/fz_bitstring_valid_utf8) as booleans; their declared integer contracts remain integer.
- Preserve result structure in the existing resolved extern contract instead of falling through to ExternTy::Any. Store no second semantic contract or independent mutable layout authority. Distinguish the fixed foreign layout from downstream Fz transport demand.
- Derive the physical C call signature from the target ABI and the full declaration. Ignoring one field, specializing a caller, or narrowing a type must not remove a physical return field or change the foreign signature.
- Do not equate C aggregate return classification with one native register of each field's source type. In particular, mixed double/word aggregates may use different register classes on x86-64 and AArch64. Verify the real C/Rust struct ABI on the project's supported targets and Linux CI; use existing backend ABI facilities where possible.
- The interpreter calls the exact concrete C aggregate-return function type, then exposes its fields through existing backend tuple/return transport. Current Prim::Extern/LowerOut/call_lowered_extern and extern-body Term::Return plumbing are scalar; extend that producer/binding seam to honestly carry both decoded results into existing BackendBoundValue::Transport/ReturnLanes. Do not feed a multi-lane contract through scalar Term::Return, synthesize a tagged Any, allocate a tuple then project it, or add a second return-layout planner. Native adapts the physical result to the same existing structural lanes. Preserve whole-value consumers: normal tuple materialization is allowed only when an actual consumer needs a whole value, never merely to cross this scalar-pair seam.
- Reuse the existing interpreter argument-shape dispatcher parameterized by return shape. Do not copy the 31 argument cases into separate handwritten dispatchers. Reject noncanonical boolean words with a shared explicit foreign-contract diagnostic rather than silently treating any nonzero word as true.
- Keep existing scalar, binary, opaque-value and variadic behavior within their supported contracts. The new by-value result spelling is required for C externs; do not silently reinterpret an existing fz-ABI value-ref return contract as a C aggregate. Retain the source semantic/result structure and an explicit foreign representation so these are not confused. New unsupported aggregate forms (larger/nested results, aggregate arguments, arrays/unions/packed layouts) are diagnosed at the shared boundary, not accepted on one door and guessed/boxed on another. A deliberately opaque Any result remains an ordinary value-ref result; it must not be confused with a by-value aggregate declaration.

## Arithmetic and panic policy

- Real arithmetic exports are total over their declared Fz input domains. Fallible operations return {result, failed}; infallible operations need no status. The runtime export never raises, unwinds, aborts for an arithmetic condition, or sets hidden process/TLS exception state.
- Use checked i64 add/subtract/multiply/negate and integer division: overflow is failure. Integer division truncates toward zero; zero divisor and MIN_I64 / -1 fail. Integer remainder takes the dividend's sign, fails for zero divisor, and MIN_I64 rem -1 succeeds with zero.
- `/` remains always floating; div/2 remains integer division. Preserve mixed numeric conversion semantics and `%`/float fmod behavior. For operations admitting failure, zero divisors and nonfinite floating results return failure; finite signed zeros/subnormals remain valid. Float negation of a valid finite Fz float is infallible. Do not import BEAM bignum promotion into this i64 language.
- On failure all returned fields are initialized and valid for their declared Fz types. For checked integer add/subtract/multiply/negate, return the wrapped i64 machine result plus true on overflow (the natural overflowing_* / CLIF result, avoiding unnecessary normalization work). For invalid integer division/remainder return {0,true}; for failed floating arithmetic return {0.0,true}. The optimized replacement must agree even when callers inspect both fields. Never return NaN/Inf and rely on examining failed after a decoder has already rejected the payload.
- Every Kernel arithmetic failure branch calls exactly one private helper: `arithmetic_error/0`, whose current body is `panic(:badarith)`. Do not duplicate panic bodies or hide failure decisions inside the C functions.
- User explicitly accepts a loud fatal panic for now. Reuse the existing panic endpoint. Require an identifiable diagnostic and no successful continuation; do NOT expand this ticket into new fault delivery, process teardown guarantees, source-stack reporting, catchability, or interpreter/REPL-host survival guarantees. Preserve behavior already provided, but do not build those capabilities as prerequisites.
- The approved fatal endpoint is intentionally separate from total arithmetic exports. Do not add arithmetic exception polling to generic foreign calls or redesign Never/panic to satisfy the superseded graceful-error plan. fz-kdt.28 owns replacing this one helper with proper language exceptions later.
- Runtime comparison exports likewise become real truthful calls, returning raw boolean without boxing. Preserve the existing comparison authority and exact mixed-number, widening-vs-strict, binary, and signed-zero semantics; do not recreate them from symbol names. Binary comparisons cannot use C's bare binary byte-pointer marshal without lengths: use the existing truthful ref-carrying fz ABI (or an already-supported exact explicit pointer/length signature), and preserve context/schema access for general value comparisons.

## Native substitution: required now

- Interpreter/REPL execution calls the real exports through generic FFI. JIT/AOT may replace eligible arithmetic/comparison calls with semantically identical scalar operations. The real function must remain callable; substitution is an optimization, not what makes the declaration exist.
- Identify an eligible call by its resolved runtime export binding and validated full physical signature, and carry that eligibility to its CLIF FuncRef/call. Never recognize a user function by a local spelling, parse `_ii`/canonical type strings, or bypass ABI validation because a symbol looks familiar. A same-name shadow or incompatible declaration must not receive the substitution.
- Replace the known extern call in CLIF (or the existing equivalent call-emission seam, without creating then repairing boxed transport) with result/status-producing arithmetic. Reuse existing scalar lowering; do not build a second compiler/optimizer subsystem or a new semantic descriptor registry.
- For add/sub/multiply use Cranelift's overflow-result operations; guard division/remainder hazards with control flow before trapping instructions (a select after sdiv/srem is insufficient); use valid finite failure payloads for floats. Keep Fz's failure branch and error helper. Prove native and real-export results agree at edges, not only ordinary values.
- The new/changed runtime-owned exports need exact physical validation as part of this ticket before unsafe calls or substitutions. Keep one physical manifest/address inventory and extend its existing representation; fz-5xp.32 completes validation for the entire runtime later. Do not create a temporary second signature table or postpone safety of this ticket's signatures to .32.
- No added arithmetic C call, scalar box, tuple box, caller-visible output pointer, or extra successful-path wrapper layer is allowed in the optimized typed arithmetic body. Float/mixed remainder is the explicit existing exception to call elimination: CLIF has no frem; retain one truthful fmod-backed runtime helper call, its scalar-pair result and the wrapper's failure branch. Do not build a new remainder algorithm or add an adapter-call chain merely to claim all arithmetic is inlined. Existing outer Fz/CPS wrapper calls remain; removing them is fz-5xp.20. Do not claim the whole source loop is call-free merely because the inner foreign call disappeared.

## Required arithmetic lowering coverage

| Runtime export family | Real result | Native treatment in this ticket |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fz_op_neg_i | {integer, boolean} | Checked negation, including MIN_I64 |
| fz_op_neg_f | float | Existing finite-float sign change |
| fz_op_add_ii, sub_ii, mul_ii | {integer, boolean} | Overflowing scalar op + flag |
| Existing add/sub/mul mixed and float variants | {float, boolean} | Exact declared conversions, scalar float op, finite-result check |
| fz_op_div_ii (div/2) | {integer, boolean} | Branch around zero and MIN_I64/-1 before sdiv |
| fz_op_div_ii_to_float and div_if/div_fi/div_ff (/) | {float, boolean} | Float division with +/-0 divisor and nonfinite-result handling |
| fz_op_rem_ii | {integer, boolean} | Zero -> failure; MIN_I64/-1 -> successful zero without executing a hazardous divide; otherwise remainder |
| fz_op_rem_if/rem_fi/rem_ff | {float, boolean} | One existing fmod-backed real helper call; no CLIF frem and no invented replacement algorithm |

The family labels abbreviate the existing exact export names; do not discover semantics by parsing these suffixes. Inventory and record every retained actual export before implementation. MIN_I64 / -1 through `/` converts to floating arithmetic and can succeed; only integer div/2 has the i64 quotient overflow failure. Cover both signs of floating zero and both fields of failed results.

## Execution order and TDD

1. Reinspect the worktree and authorities below; baseline the existing successful-path call/allocation counts and retained-product reuse. Inventory all affected exports/boolean signatures and write the declared-C-layout-to-Fz-lanes examples before editing.
2. Add a RED ordinary non-arithmetic extern fixture returning a scalar pair. Prove the actual foreign call before enabling any arithmetic substitution. Cover word/word, float/word, word/float and float/float physical families, false/true fields, ignored fields, private captured/aliased foreign callables, and whole-tuple consumers. Derive aliases through resolved Ty, not token/rendered-name matches.
3. Implement the shared scalar-boolean and fixed-pair foreign layout/adapters on interpreter, JIT and AOT. Use exact prototype C or repr(C) fixtures as the ABI oracle. Verify each supported semantic pairing and target classification (including pure target-layout tests for x86-64 SysV and AArch64/AAPCS64, plus actual host execution); fail unsupported shapes consistently. Keep all currently affected declarations/exports coherent in the working tree.
4. RED-test real total arithmetic exports at zero/overflow/extreme/finite boundaries; implement one runtime owner. Change Kernel declarations and wrappers to result/status and the single arithmetic_error helper. Update comparisons and exact export registration in the same cutover.
5. RED-test native call elimination, scalar lane preservation, zero allocation, and equivalence with direct real calls. Implement validated CLIF substitution using existing arithmetic lowering. Keep a bounded test route that forces a real call and compares both returned fields; do not add a permanent user-facing optimization toggle merely for tests.
6. Finish/revalidate existing private-extern, process export, resource, spawn/send, binary concatenation and spawn_opt deletion work. Retain only scheduler callbacks actually required by ordinary fz ABI execution; don't extend them into arithmetic error channels.
7. Delete replaced interpreter shims, fake exports, old native intercept chains, aliases, duplicate contracts/effect guesses, migrated tests and stale docs in this commit. Broaden verification only after focused proof is green.

## Acceptance signals

- Ordinary user-defined private foreign fixtures use the same scalar-pair return rule; no arithmetic name is needed. All affected scalar-boolean exports match their declaration and do not allocate merely to return true/false.
- Interpreter, forced real native call, optimized JIT and AOT agree on both result and status. Cover overflow, zero divisors, MIN/-1 division and remainder, mixed inputs, floating overflow/finite values, and returning/destructuring/ignoring fields. Also test an arithmetic expression whose successful value is unused: a failure must still reach arithmetic_error rather than being erased by demand/DCE. Test fatal wrapper behavior in subprocesses so the permitted loud panic cannot kill the test harness.
- Successful typed arithmetic proves zero added scalar/tuple allocations and no arithmetic foreign call in inline-supported optimized bodies; float/mixed remainder retains only its documented single helper call. Whole-tuple escape follows existing materialization rules. Preserve native comparison allocation pins and existing wrapper-call budget.
- Same input reuses World/ProductMemo results with unchanged allocations/generations and no extra compiler work; unrelated edits do not invalidate the requested root. No global export/type inventory rescan is introduced on warm requests. Use existing telemetry/transport tests and only necessary additional observations.
- Full relevant library/fixture/CLI/AOT suites, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace --all-features pass; verify Linux CI's physical ABI as well as local targets. Do not use an earlier pre-rebase pass as evidence for this candidate.
- Update .agent/docs/externs.md, semantic-authorities.md, affected transport/process docs and guides/externs.html with the retained model, the exact boolean/aggregate C ABI, total arithmetic, temporary panic endpoint and later owners. Remove one-shot negative source scans after they have served their migration purpose; retain meaningful behavioral/ABI tests. Remove construction probes and duplicated fixture execution.

## Boundaries and successor order

- fz-tfn.69 is completed history, not a reason to restart stack repair. .30 does not become a prerequisite for fz-tfn.62.
- .30 -> fz-5xp.32: close the entire runtime physical-export manifest only after final names, booleans and result aggregates exist. .30 already validates the new signatures it calls.
- .32 -> fz-5xp.20: later ordinary-wrapper inlining, including the status case, with no foreign/source ABI change.
- .32 -> fz-kdt.28: later replace arithmetic_error's fatal panic with proper language exception handling. No graceful-error framework is required now.
- .32 -> fz-5xp.37: later complete the existing extern argument-shape coverage, reusing this ticket's aggregate tests and exact prototypes.
- Larger/nested aggregates and aggregate arguments are future API expansion, not construction debris needed for this cutover. Preserve typed structure and one ABI adapter so extension adds layouts rather than an alternative return system. Do not implement arrays/unions/public-extern policy here.
- fz-5xp.35 and fz-kdt.164 own existing wrong-F64-argument diagnosis/runtime enforcement; fz-5xp.61 owns library naming. Do not silently absorb those separate bugs. If one actually blocks this contract, resolve its existing ticket and ordering before further construction.

## Starting state and references

Planning inspection on 2026-09-13: candidate worktree /private/tmp/fz-5xp30-world (also accessible through /tmp), branch fz-5xp.30/world-terminal-authority, HEAD 4f49465f9bbf1986f1b1ccae0a9827b7faa3dfe1, 92 modified/deleted/untracked paths. .30 is not committed. HEAD contains predecessor ticket commits; branch upstream must be verified rather than used blindly for push. A safety autostash exists at object 2e8fdbe5f; do not apply/drop it by mutable stash index or overwrite the candidate. Verify current state and editing ownership before resuming. The candidate was replayed onto main's boolean rename; post-rebase tests still need to run.

Read AGENTS.md, .agent/strategies.md and strategies/output-contract-loop.md. Existing authorities: src/extern_contract.rs; compiler2/jobs/body.rs resolve_extern_signature/extern_wire_ty; fz_ir::ExternDecl; compiler2/artifact.rs BackendReturnLayout; compiler2/jobs/transport.rs; compiler2/transport_contract_test.rs; compiler2/jobs/native.rs return_lane_vars; compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs emit_return_lanes; native_codegen/prim.rs lower_extern_generic/lower_arith_binop and old ARITH_SHIMS; ir_interp/extern_call.rs dispatch_shapes; ir_interp/backend.rs return decoding; runtime/src/lib.rs existing panic; runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs; lib/kernel.fz.

Research: Cranelift 0.131 supports sadd_overflow/ssub_overflow/smul_overflow with scalar result and flag. ../otp/erts/emulator/beam/jit/{x86,arm}/instr_arith.cpp shows inline hot arithmetic and cold fallback; pointer-out integer division belongs to slow C helper paths, not the hot addition model. A local clang probe of {int64_t,uint64_t} checked add returned x0/x1 on macOS ARM64 and rax/rdx on macOS x86-64 with no result allocation; this does not prove mixed aggregates or Linux and those still require actual verification.

## Delivery

Use a suitably powered implementation subagent; review with a fresh cold gpt-5.6-sol/high agent scoped to this ticket. Astra requires explicit permission. Before construction, present verified facts and the attack plan; do not reopen settled decisions merely to expand scope. One ticket, one reviewed commit, one close. Inspect the exact branch-root diff, create/update the correctly stacked draft PR using gh stacks, and push the completed ticket promptly after local gates and required predecessor CI checks. Preserve a PR the user has marked ready. No unrelated worktree edits or construction beyond this ticket without its normal discussion.
title: Make Kernel externs truthful and keep arithmetic total and unboxed
